profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Google | CS @ CMU
profile.summary:
Software Developer, Mentor, Researcher, Team Player. I am excited to take my strong background in Computer Science and apply that to software development in the industry in order to help develop new and interesting technologies.

I specialize in software and full stack development, as well as a multitude of programming languages. However, I am most proficient in Python, C, and HTML. I take pride in my ability to make collaboration fun and productive, while also making sure that all team members are on track to meet their deadlines. I am also a good listener and communicator because of my various experiences designing programs for clients and teaching students.

I am inspired by creativity, perseverance, motivation to make a change, and the resolve to always deliver results. In applying these values to my work ethic, I've become a workaholic of sorts. I can't bring myself to give up on a task once I've started and I always have to see my projects to an end. As a result, others can always count on me to deliver results.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Returned to the Supply Chain Optimization Technologies (SCOT) org as part of the Consumer Instock Value team

positions.title: Software Development Engineer Intern
positions.description: Returned to the inventory control team to develop more features for the internal auditing tool used by the corresponding science team. Developed the feature to run automated simulations with the click of a button so that the scientists wouldn't have to waste so much time doing each step manually. Created a button on the frontend that could make a call to the backend to trigger the simulation. Worked mainly with python, java, and many AWS tools like S3, DynamoDB, Step Functions, SQS, and Lambda Functions.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer Intern
positions.description: Worked on the inventory control team to develop new features for an internal auditing tool used by the corresponding science team. Developed automated generation of new data for the new features that weren't supported yet. Worked on the frontend and backend of the auditing tool to give the user access to the new features and the new data that was generated. Worked mainly with SQL, XML Scripts, Angular, HTML, Scala, and Java.

positions.title: 15-122 Teaching Assistant
positions.description: 15-122 is one of the largest and most interdisciplinary computer science courses offered at CMU. Mentor students of all computer science backgrounds and majors. Play an integral part of making sure that the semester goes by smoothly by attending weekly grading meetings, teaching a programming lab every week, and holding weekly office hours.

company.name: Carnegie Mellon University School of Computer Science

positions.title: Student Researcher
positions.description: Worked as a student researcher in the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. Reviewed shell scripts for older product and converted into python scripts for the 2.0 product. Applied new methods defined in the Swagger API into the new python scripts.

positions.title: Full Stack Developer - Intern
positions.description: Tackled the challenge of familiarizing myself with new programming languages and frameworks like Typescript and Angular. Developed the user onboarding pages on the v 2.0 website from scratch and ensured successful transfer of data between frontend and backend. Involved myself in the SaaS (Software as a Service) product development process.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Developed and refined the program for the Smart Maker Reflection Booth as part of the NSF-funded Smart Making Spaces Project. Programmed a customer-friendly interface for the Smart Maker Reflection Booth. This interface focused on walking the customer through an extensive self-reflection process. Improved communication skills through constant meetings with the clients.

company.name: Human-Computer Interaction Institute - Carnegie Mellon University - School of Computer Science

positions.title: Tutor / Teacher
positions.description: Applied knowledge gained from achieving A's in Calculus BC, AP Biology, and AP Physics to teach younger students the material from these courses. Created personalized curriculums for each student and either taught them new material in the relevant subject, or enforced the material that they were already learning in school. Became accustomed with the process of mentoring others.

positions.title: Internship Trainee
positions.description: Learned about the technologies that Cisco works with and develops. Shadowed full-time workers and gained insight into the work environment at Cisco. Developed and pitched IoT solutions in smart cities to the program mentors and Larry Payne, Senior Vice President of the U.S. Public Sector at Cisco.

educations.schoolName: Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology

honors.title: National AP Scholar
honors.description: Granted to students in the United States who achieve grades of 3.0, 3 or higher on at least eight full-year AP Exams, and whose average AP Exam grade is at least 4.0.

honors.title: National Merit Scholar
honors.description: The highest-achieving students in the National Merit Scholarship Program are designated as National Merit Scholars. Finalists and Semifinalists are also given recognition for their academic and extracurricular achievements.

projects.title: MotionLab
projects.description: In this project, I created an XR game that utilized the leap motion sensor to track the movement of the hands so that the user could interact with objects in the 3D virtual space. The purpose of this game was to aid in in the accessibility of high school science experiments by minimizing costs and danger. The client for this project was the PittBio Outreach program located in Pittsburgh.

projects.title: Developing Motion Tracking for Robot Application
projects.description: Utilized OpenCV to track key points of a person’s hand through motions. Kept track of the motions for these motions so a robot arm could recognize these motions and replicate them

publications.title: “Understanding Social Technology Competence and Digital Collaboration: From the Perspective of First-Generation College Students”
